executiveSummary: GM0385 passes the deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, 37,140 residents, 29 neighbourhoods, ten BAG places, eleven BRT settlement labels and first-72-hour arithmetic are coherent. The current engine also correctly restricts its six unqualified NWB links to mobility and supply: exact live NWB queries confirm the generated N247, A7, N509 and N244 section labels, and no public road is used as power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility topology. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Eight materially different nonzero hazards reuse the exact same 29-neighbourhood order, led by De Watering, and a controlled direct-fire source inside Warder leaves Warder fourteenth. This conflicts with local public evidence for Volendam-Oude kom, Rokersgracht/Burgemeester Boelenspark, Broeckgouw/Zeestraat, the Zeevang water system and outside-dike Slobbeland. The generic coastal screen creates 1.401089 normalized inundation stress, critical pressure and 24,752 affected residents at T+24 without selecting a Markermeer level, wind setup, named defence event, connected footprint, arrival or recession; at T+72 its forcing is zero but the UI still shows about 6.6K residents under pressure and exact recovering service values. The browser exposes all eleven layers without runtime errors, yet it labels this result derived-screening rather than municipality-specific unsupported and provides no Edam-Volendam operational-use warning. Public CBS/PDOK, NWB, HHNK/HWH, RWS, KNMI, NDW, provider, telecom, education and facility sources can materially improve typed context. Observations, registers, planning scenarios and simulation outputs must stay distinct; a missing station, facility, provider result or pixel remains Unknown rather than zero or safe.

evidenceSources.title: Uitvoeringsplan Klimaatadaptatie Edam-Volendam — definitive version
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive, 16 December 2021; implementation horizon 2022–2024 and climate horizon 2050
supports: The local 70 mm/hour assessment says Edam generally experiences relatively little rainwater nuisance because of surface water and that smaller cores are less paved, but identifies the low, narrow and densely built old Volendam centre as extra sensitive, with many roads impassable and possible building exposure. It also identifies Rokersgracht and Burgemeester Boelenspark locations with more than 20 cm modeled water.

The plan identifies combined-sewer nuisance pathways in Edam old centre/Zuid/Singelwijk and Volendam old centre/Rozetten/Blokgouw/Katham/Planetenbuurt, plus Oosthuizen. A long-duration 100 mm in two days event was not analysed in the cited study and therefore remains unknown, not zero.

Its PET context identifies Broeckgouw and the Zeestraat/old-centre area as heat hotspots and flags movable bridges between Edam and Volendam as potentially vulnerable during extreme heat. Other rural cores have a smaller modeled heat effect.

Drought is treated as accumulated seasonal water deficit rather than a single 72-hour pulse. Edam-Oude kom and Volendam-Oude kom have subsidence/foundation and road/sewer sensitivity; the plan also notes potential cracks in electricity infrastructure. This planning susceptibility is not a current observation or outage.

The flood assessment distinguishes regional-defence and primary-defence failure, identifies Lange Weeren southwest of Volendam in a regional-defence case, and notes possible telecom-mast and municipal sewer-pump exposure. It also records version and coverage limitations, including a then-outdated Broeckgouw elevation and a separate future rural-area workstream.

The PDF is static planning/model evidence, not a warning, forecast, observed event or live asset state. It offers no stable machine API, fixed refresh cadence or explicit standalone permissive licence for its underlying rasters; obtain owner-authorized native exports with event, units, resolution, edition, lineage, licence and NoData before causal ingestion.

evidenceSources.title: Markermeer high-water protocol, Slobbeland outside-dike exposure and current local water projects
evidenceSources.edition: Live municipal protocol and HHNK project pages inspected 2 September 2026; project dates and status are valid-time context
supports: The municipality says Slobbeland lies outside the dike and that small level rises can cause nuisance, damage and evacuation of public space, with homes and businesses potentially evacuated in extreme cases. Its protocol distinguishes below -0.10 m NAP, -0.10 to 0.00, 0.00 to +0.10, +0.10 to +0.40 with onshore wind, and above +0.40 with onshore wind; actions include monitoring, WMCN contact, road/parking closure, a tractor pump, sandbags and possible evacuation.

The same page says outside-dike parking is cleared at +0.10 m and makes onshore wind part of escalation. These threshold/action rules are human-readable operational context, not a general hydraulic surface or permission to infer that every municipality neighbourhood shares one depth.

HHNK's current local page https://www.hhnk.nl/werk-in-de-buurt-edam-volendam identifies the De Worst sewer pump and Volendam pressure main, Zeevang regional-defence improvement, and the 33 km Markermeer-dike strengthening programme. Its project pages are status context; a historic failure-to-meet-norm statement, completed work or planned work must be retained with valid time and never converted into current failure or guaranteed performance.

HHNK's Zeevang project page https://www.hhnk.nl/verbetering-boezemkade-polder-zeevang distinguishes sections from Edam via Kwadijk and Hobrede to Oosthuizen and records differing height/macrostability work and schedules. It provides no event-specific breach, current condition telemetry or T+72 recession/restoration path.

The live pages state no standard machine-data licence or fixed refresh cadence. Use them as timestamped policy/project context; bind a real exercise only to WMCN/RWS/HHNK valid-time water levels, forecasts, defence state and authorized incident decisions.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 with older detailed 2021–2024 scenario evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current statutory profile 2025–2028; older detailed 2021–2024 PDF used only where explicitly labelled historical
supports: The current profile at https://vrzw.publiqa.online/regionaal-risicoprofiel/overzicht-risicos covers 22 incident types and distinguishes prolonged drought, extreme rainfall/Markermeer-IJsselmeer levels, fire, long gas-supply outage, cyber/vital-infrastructure disruption and cascading service consequences. Scenario descriptions are illustrative regional planning context, not forecasts or GM0385 probabilities.

The current developments section describes increasing extreme rain, drought and heat, nature/roadside fire, dike cracks, higher water/electricity demand, and cyber cascades that can reach electricity and hospitals. It does not calibrate the simulator's exact municipality values, dependency coefficients or restoration durations.

The superseded detailed profile https://www.veiligheidsregiozaanstreekwaterland.nl/fileadmin/user_upload/Regionaal_Risicoprofiel_VrZW_2021-2024_Beleidsdocument.pdf records a Warder M2.5 earthquake in June 2018 at about 3 km depth, likely induced by gas extraction, and a Kwadijk M2.7 event in 1989; its illustrative local scenario is M2.4 with minor building damage and public concern. This is evidence for a local seismic source family, not current shaking or a prediction.

That older profile also provides a detailed preventive-evacuation and dike-failure planning case with roughly 35,000 evacuees and 48 hours lead time, followed by multi-day rescue and longer recovery. Its edition is obsolete for current policy but demonstrates that exact evacuation/recovery requires named scenario and resource assumptions rather than a generic coastal distance scalar.

The profile is a statutory planning publication without a machine hazard API, fixed operational cadence or explicit standard reuse licence. Retain edition and illustrative status and obtain current authority-selected scenario/resource inputs before operational use.

supports: The integration-ready national OGC APIs are CC BY-SA 4.0: IMWA water-control works at the cited URL and DAMO water chain at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1. Exact point-in-polygon intersection with the consumed GM0385 geometry finds 226 displayed records: 14 sewer pumps, one wastewater treatment plant, 136 surface-water pumps, six sluices and 69 weirs. Named records include Rg. Volendam, Rg. Slobbeland, Rg. De Worst and rwzi Oosthuizen.

Normalized register capacities include 800 for Rg. Volendam, 49 for Rg. Slobbeland and 77 for Rg. De Worst, but the display export omits a safely comparable unit and the status 'gerealiseerd' does not prove current operation. HHNK separately says De Worst pumps to treatment at Katwoude, illustrating cross-boundary service dependence that point containment cannot reconstruct.

The HHNK climate atlas https://hhnk.klimaatmonitor.net/ provides a public visualization/catalogue, while downloads for some native rasters require owner permission or login. Map products are orientation/planning context; licence, scenario, edition, resolution, units and NoData must be checked per layer.

LIWO OWS https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows and API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 expose named/versioned depth, arrival and duration products for expert scenario selection. Verify each product's water-system family, failed/intact defence assumption, units, probability, resolution, licence/terms and NoData; no blanket causal selection is safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / KNMI / NDW / RDI / DUO / KVK / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: Valid-time water, weather, road and seismic feeds with telecom, education, government and acute-care registers
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public-context snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026; each observation retains its own valid time
supports: RWS Waterinfo is an integration-ready CC0 public API whose LMW measurements are generally produced every ten minutes and response is cached five minutes; it is explicitly non-mission-critical. GM0385 has one assigned Edam point at -28 cm NAP observed 2026-09-02T17:30:00Z, 33 minutes old at retrieval. It is a point observation on its own clock, not a continuous hydraulic surface, WMCN forecast, breach or arbitrary T+72 state.

KNMI Data Platform https://developer.dataplatform.knmi.nl/ exposes product-specific observations/forecasts, commonly CC BY 4.0, with radar products at roughly five-minute cadence; FDSN https://rdsa.knmi.nl/fdsnws/event/1 is automatically updated and defaults to CC BY 4.0. The deployed 365-day seismic snapshot has no event assigned inside GM0385. That is catalogue/time-window NoData, not zero seismic hazard.

NDW DATEX II https://opendata.ndw.nu/actueel_beeld.xml.gz is integration-ready CC0 valid-time road-event data. The deployed snapshot has no event point inside GM0385; no record cannot prove every road open now and can never define an arbitrary scenario T+72 state without aligned reference and validity time.

RDI WFS https://antenneregister.nl/mapserver/wfs/ contributes 54 in-boundary antenna-installation records; its service states no fees/access constraints but no standard reuse licence or fixed refresh cadence. DUO RIO https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/dataset/c416acd1-e083-4ec6-9203-3b20f98fe143 contributes 20 education locations, updates daily around 06:15 and uses an attribution licence whose version is unspecified. KVK/PDOK Public Domain OGC https://api.pdok.nl/kvk/overheidsdiensten-geharmoniseerd/ogc/v1 contributes 12 governmental-service points, six public-administration and six public-order/safety records.

RIVM acute-care 2026 v1.1 is versioned CC0 at https://datacatalogus.rivm.nl/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.21945/8E767B2D-9CED-4A85-A95D-3AC1A608C663 and returns no in-boundary emergency department; the RIVM PM2.5 snapshot likewise has no station. These are coverage-limited no-match results, not proof of no healthcare need, no external care dependence, clean air, open access, staffing or incident capacity.

Every observed feed, registry and planning product must preserve publisher, retrieval, observation/valid time, edition, licence, spatial coverage and quality. Only an explicitly time-aligned exercise adapter may let a current observation affect a run; otherwise affectsSimulation remains false.

notes: Peak municipality severities are storm 0.638663, pluvial 0.274384, river 0, coastal 0.496194, heat 0.607402, winter 0.448066, cyber 0.426536, earthquake 0.038476, wildfire 0.149164 and compound 0.864172.

The canonical major-river screen produces exact zero event forcing and event-attributable person-hours for GM0385. That is a scoped result for the named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel screen, not an all-clear for Markermeer, regional-defence, polder or pluvial mechanisms.

All weather, water, fire, earthquake and cyber values are deterministic exercise assumptions, not observations, probabilities, warnings, attack intelligence, outage reports or forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, cumulative burden, route bounds, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass on the current engine.

The canonical coastal T+24 produces 1.401089 normalized flood stress but selects no Markermeer level, onshore-wind threshold, failed/overtopped defence, outside-dike mask, connected footprint, depth, arrival, duration or recession.

GM0385 has no municipality-specific unsupported-spatial note in packages/sim-core/src/model.ts, so the browser renders precise local values and derived-screening water headlines without a local audit warning.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipal ledgers close and expose evidence class, dependency order, operational assumptions and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; every service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; weighted service shortfalls sum to municipal pressure.
System-pressure weights are power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12, totaling one.
Dependency chains, local-context factors, drivers, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.

Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences rather than physical fragility. Day type, start clock, demand, backup, network and repair multipliers are normalized and labeled scenario assumptions; interventions are response-delayed and do not masquerade as actual Edam-Volendam crews or assets.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure relative to a matched no-event baseline before intermunicipal transfers and apply a preparedness multiplier. They are a modeled pre-transfer burden proxy, not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

No selected Markermeer event, water recession, road/pump/control state, backup, crew, material or repair plan supports that exact path.

The model's sustained-water repair guard prevents instant repair, but the standing-water magnitude and duration are themselves uncalibrated.

E03–E06 support multi-hour water, pump, sewer, defence, outside-dike and access dependencies; E05's older evacuation case illustrates multi-day consequences. None selects this event or commits actual local response resources.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Edam-Volendam disaster, outage, evacuation, casualty, health, welfare or restoration dataset.

The CBS 2025 generalized boundary supports municipal aggregation but not parcel hydraulics, outside-dike footprints, polder compartments, drainage catchments, defence zones, asset ownership, utility zones, road approaches or incident perimeters.

The 2021 climate plan is strong local modeled/planning evidence but its underlying native stress-test/heat/drought rasters, exact current metadata and permissive reuse terms are not exposed through a reviewed machine API. Historical/planning outputs must not be relabeled observations.

The current VRZW 2025–2028 profile supplies mechanism/cascade context, not local forcing, probabilities, live state, resource inventories or restoration promises; the detailed 2021–2024 scenarios are explicitly superseded historical planning evidence.
Municipal and HHNK project/status pages are valid-time context. Historic non-compliance, planned strengthening and completed work do not establish a defence's current event performance.
LIWO products require expert event/version/licence/NoData selection and do not independently provide current defence condition, outside-dike response, drainage controls or recovery resources.

HWH IMWA/DAMO is partial provider-supplied inventory; point counts, normalized capacities and register status do not establish comparable units, connectivity, direction, control, operation, power/backup or service delivery.

NWB/ProRail/GTFS and a no-match NDW snapshot do not provide internal streets, bridge/road/ferry/bus operation, evacuation throughput, emergency access or future passability. Repeated A7 source sections are series provenance and not additive capacity.

Provider/capacity/antenna/school/government/care/station records are partial dated context, not complete topology, current load, capacity, occupancy, radio coverage, backup, stocks, access or restoration commitment.
No reviewed safe public source supplies complete Liander, PWN, wastewater, gas, telecom/backhaul, facility, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; security-sensitive detail was not inferred.

First-72-hour household behavior, medical dependence, visitors, responders, mutual aid, shelters, evacuation vehicles, pharmacies, fuel/food stocks, pump controls, crew travel and repair priorities remain scenario assumptions or Unknown.
